uutiset.t: New York MTA’s Budget Risks $1 Billion Shortfall in 2030
uutiset.s: New York City’s transit system is projecting a nearly $1 billion budget gap in 2030 as increasing health care and fuel costs outpace its revenue growth.

Did Nvidia’s board move too soon in ruling out Jensen Huang’s return? New Street Tech Infrastructure Analyst Antoine Chkaiban joined Bloomberg Open Interest to argue that the decision could hurt shareholders, employees, and Nvidia’s long-term edge. (Source: Bloomberg)

uutiset.t: Credit Selloff Lures Bargain Hunters to ‘Stock Picker’s Market’
uutiset.s: Credit has become a hunting ground for investors brave enough to swoop in on beaten-up securities.

uutiset.t: Blackstone’s Jon Gray Calls Concerns About AI Bubble Overblown
uutiset.s: Blackstone Inc. President Jon Gray reiterated his view that fears of a bubble in artificial intelligence are overblown and that AI infrastructure supply still lags far behind demand.

uutiset.t: NYC Comptroller ‘Not Done Fighting Yet’ on Anthropic IPO
uutiset.s: New York City Comptroller Mark Levine called it ‘disappointing” that Anthropic is moving ahead with its initial public offering this week despite calls for the company to pause the listing over AI safety concerns. He speaks on “Bloomberg Surveillance.” (Source: Bloomberg)

uutiset.t: Brookfield Bets $110 Million That RV Resorts Have Staying Power
uutiset.s: Brookfield Asset Management is investing $110 million into a company that’s rolling up independent campgrounds in a bet that a pandemic-era surge in outdoor hospitality has staying power.

uutiset.t: Nike Bets on Cricket to Triple India Sales as China Sputters
uutiset.s: Nike Inc. is targeting a booming sports market dominated by cricket to triple its India business in five years, as growth falters in Greater China.

uutiset.t: Odd Lots: GTA VI Is the Most Expensive Game Ever Made. Is It Worth It?
uutiset.s: The much anticipated Grand Theft Auto VI will be released on November 19 as the most expensive video game ever made. Bloomberg News video game reporter Jason Schreier joins Joe Weisenthal and Tracy Alloway on the Odd Lots podcast to discuss why it took 13 years and reportedly over $1 billion to make

uutiset.t: Turkey Slaps Main Erdogan Rival Imamoglu With Political Ban
uutiset.s: A Turkish court ordered a political ban for Istanbul Mayor Ekrem Imamoglu, President Recep Tayyip Erdogan’s main opponent, paving the way for the ruling party to potentially take control of Turkey’s largest city.

uutiset.t: Stocks Waver After Nvidia Results as Anthropic IPO Test Looms
uutiset.s: US technology stocks edged higher in the wake of Nvidia Corp.’s earnings, while traders looked to the mammoth market debut of Anthropic PBC for the next key test of the artificial intelligence trade.

uutiset.t: Lithium CEO Warns of Perils Facing US Critical Minerals Push
uutiset.s: Lithium Americas Corp.’s flagship US mine has become an expensive test of the Trump administration’s push to rebuild a domestic critical minerals industry, with labor shortages, rising wages and tariffs pushing its construction bill almost $900 million higher.

uutiset.t: Credit Chiefs Warn of ‘Fear Factor’ as Debt Reprices All at Once
uutiset.s: A sharp repricing across fixed-income markets in recent months is likely to continue as interest rates remain elevated, causing a shakeout among weaker borrowers across industries.

uutiset.t: BASF’s Evonik Chase Poses Test for Potential Merz Successor
uutiset.s: BASF SE’s bid to consolidate Germany’s struggling chemicals industry with a takeover of Evonik Industries AG looks set to join the ranks of politically-charged deals taking shape across Europe this year.

uutiset.t: Treasuries Higher for a Third Day as Risk Appetite Ebbs
uutiset.s: Benchmark US Treasuries rose for a third day with support from setbacks for US stocks, falling oil prices and speculation that most of the Federal Reserve’s upcoming interest-rate hikes are already priced in.

uutiset.t: Copper Plunges Over 5% as AI Trade Unravels in Metals Markets
uutiset.s: Copper plunged in a broad selloff across London, New York and Shanghai, as bullish investors bailed on bets tied to the AI boom and others turned outright bearish even as extreme squeezes roil metals markets.
